scenes.caption: Adding fractions
scenes.narration: Let's add one half and one quarter. Watch how a quarter fits inside a half - exactly twice.

shape.explain: The question: 1/2 + 1/4 = ?
The first bar: one whole.
The blue half: 1/2 of the bar.
The label: half of the bar is blue.
The second bar: one whole.
The green quarter: 1/4 of the bar.
The label: a quarter of the bar is green.

steps.text: A quarter fits inside a half, exactly twice

scenes.caption: Make the pieces the same size
scenes.narration: We cannot add halves and quarters directly. Watch the blade split the half - now every piece is a quarter.

shape.explain: The whole bar: it holds one half.
The half: it must be cut before it can add.
The label: 1/2.
The blade: it cuts the half into two quarters - now every piece is the same size.
One of the two new quarters: the cut half became two quarters.
One of the two new quarters: the cut half became two quarters.
The conversion: 1/2 = 2/4.

steps.text: Now every piece is a quarter - add the quarters

scenes.caption: Count the quarters
scenes.narration: Two quarters plus one quarter is three quarters. The bottom number stays 4 because the piece size never changed.

shape.explain: The answer frame: it gathers the quarters.
One of the three quarters: two from the converted half plus one more make three quarters.
One of the three quarters: two from the converted half plus one more make three quarters.
One of the three quarters: two from the converted half plus one more make three quarters.
The counting zone: three quarters fit inside it.
The addition: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.
The wrong turn 3/8?: it adds the bottoms too - but pieces stay quarters.

shape.text: The bottoms never add - pieces stay quarters
shape.explain: The rule: the bottoms never add - pieces stay quarters.

scenes.caption: Watch out: 1/2 + 1/4 is not 2/6
scenes.narration: Watch out: the tempting wrong turn is adding the tops and bottoms, so 1/2 + 1/4 becomes 2/6. The bottom number names the piece size, so it cannot be added like the tops. The bottom number stays 4 because the piece size never changed: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4.

shape.explain: The comparison bar: it shows both addends.
One of the three quarter cells: the final three quarters.
One of the three quarter cells: the final three quarters.
One of the three quarter cells: the final three quarters.

shape.text: Same size -> add tops, keep bottom
shape.explain: The rule card: same size - add the tops, keep the bottom.
The rule card: different sizes - convert first, then add.
The answer card: 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4.
